The Bureau of Land Management is responsible for the management of 452 million acres of national resource lands located primarily in the eleven western States and Alaska. The national resource lands comprise sixty percent of all federally-owned land and twenty percent of America's total land base. The Bureau applies multiple-use principles in the management of its lands and generally considers the national resource lands open to public use unless closed for a specific reason. The wise use of the land and water from which these resources and benefits are derived is the overriding premise on which the Bureau's management programs are founded. In implementing Executive Order 11644, the Bureau will evaluate through its planning system, all of its lands to determine if they should remain open to ORV use with certain restrictions or closed to such use. Public participation will be solicited on each area prior to its designation as open (with controls) or closed to ORV use. An environmental analysis will also be prepared to evaluate the effects of the action. ORV use will be confined to areas and trails that have been designated as open to their use, and in such locales will be subject to certain controls.
Such areas and trails will be selected on lands having terrain suitable to vehicle capability and having low vegetative production, erosion, and siltation potentials. Selection shall be governed by the ability of the land and resources to withstand various types of ORV use.
The mission of the <u>Bureau of Reclamation</u> includes the development of water resources for the western States. Thus, some 250 recreational areas on Reclamation projects in the 17 Western States include over 3.7 million acres of land and 1.5 million acres of water that are available for public recreation use. Currently, annual use approximates 55 million visitor days for a wide variety of activities, including ORV use. Recreational administration of most of these areas has been assumed by other Federal and non-Federal agencies under formal agreements with the <u>Bureau</u>. ORV use will be limited to those areas for which appropriate regulations are implemented to control such use in a manner consistent with other recreation activities, needs for erosion control, needs for vegetative protection, needs for wildlife protection, and requirements relating to other authorized project purposes (i.e., irrigation, flood control, power production, etc.).
II. Environmental Impact of the Proposed Action
The Secretary's memorandum and Interior Bureau's regulations would implement Executive Order 11644 on all public lands managed by the Department of the Interior. Implementation of these directives will affect all phases of public land administration, the public, ORV user and non-user groups and ORV industries. Further, many resource interests will be affected. Provisions of the United States Mining Laws will apply as appropriate to the exploration of minerals, prospecting, and oil and gas geophysical exploration on Interior lands.
